ai.description: This slender sea snake reaches 1 meter. It is grey or bluish-grey above with dark crossbands and a pale belly. Key features include a small head and 40–50 scale rows around the midbody.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hydrophis caerulescens* is best distinguished by its 15–17 scale rows around the neck, which is significantly fewer than the 25–35 rows found in most similar sea snakes.
ai.habitat: The Dwarf Sea Snake inhabits shallow coastal waters and estuaries of the Indian subcontinent, often frequenting muddy or sandy sea floors near mangrove ecosystems.
ai.behavior: The dwarf sea snake is primarily nocturnal, spending its nights actively hunting for small fish and crustaceans along the seafloor in shallow coastal waters.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hydrophis caerulescens* is viviparous, giving birth to live young. It typically produces litters of 2–6 offspring, with breeding occurring during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Dwarf Sea Snake occurs in coastal waters along the Indian subcontinent, ranging from the Arabian Sea to the Bay of Bengal, including the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
